ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.74 for the unexempted detour distance on the two off-route segments; issue as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 and remind the driver of the RD-1 shortest-route obligation.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 22:57–23:03 adds 1.14 km (2.63 km driven vs 1.50 km optimal, up to 970 m off the optimal route). No passenger-named stop or reroute in chat [F8][F9] (RD-3), no pre-departure driver proposal accepted by the rider (RD-5), and driver's GPS-reroute claim [F10] lacks traffic support: bands are only band 3 [F11][F12] and no incidents were recorded [F13] (RD-4). Unexempted under RD-1; refundable under RD-2.

Off-route segment 23:21–23:24 adds 1.51 km (1.65 km driven vs 0.14 km optimal, up to 985 m off the optimal route). Same analysis: no rider-directed routing (RD-3), no prior agreed route change (RD-5), and no qualifying traffic cause — band 3 only and no incidents [F11][F12][F13] (RD-4). Unexempted under RD-1; refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's 'GPS rerouted me' statement is a bare claim; it conflicts with the GPS/timeline and fare records and is unsupported by any traffic incident or band 1–2 congestion on the replaced optimal segment [F11][F12][F13], so it fails RD-4 and is overridden by system records.
The 0.45 km gap between the billed excess distance (3.1 km, $4.41) and the sum of unexempted segment extras (2.65 km) is map-matching residue and is expressly not refundable under RD-2.
